results.title: Intern Lumina U2: Local VRAM and Hardware Fit
results.content: Released under an Apache 2.0 license, the model provides an alternative to fragmented local multimodal stacks. Shanghai AI Lab published weights trained on both Huawei Ascend NPUs and NVIDIA GPUs, establishing broad hardware compatibility across research and edge deployment environments. By eliminating the architectural division between generation and perception, Intern Lumina U2 allows local practitioners to run text-to-image generation alongside deep visual document extraction from a single set of shared model weights. [...] Intern Lumina U2 vs InternVL-U: InternVL-U relies on dense parameter activations and separate vision-encoder stacks. While InternVL-U performs reliably on core text document recognition, Intern Lumina U2 demonstrates markedly superior performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (36.5 vs 22.1 on MathVision; 63.6 vs 46.97 on DynaMath) and chart parsing (85.9 vs 53.3 on CharXiv-DQ). Intern Lumina U2 also natively generates and edits imagery, which InternVL-U cannot do without external pipeline tooling. [...] Intern Lumina U2 vs LLaDA2.0-Uni: LLaDA2.0-Uni is a strong contender in all-in-one architectures, matching Intern Lumina U2's 89 GenEval score. However, Intern Lumina U2 outclasses LLaDA2.0-Uni in visual hallucination suppression (64.6 vs 50.2 on HallusionBench) and visual mathematical processing (36.5 vs 26.7 on MathVision). Furthermore, its 8-codebook AToken configuration prevents degradation in granular visual detail during local text-to-image synthesis.

results.content:
## 🌟 Introduction

Intern Lumina U2 is a unified multimodal model that brings language, image, video and 3D into a single framework, covering text QA, text-to-image generation, image understanding, image editing, video understanding and 3D understanding with one model. It is a 16.9B-parameter MoE with ~1.4B active parameters, pairing an efficient sparse backbone with an 8-codebook fully-discrete visual representation built on AToken. [...] Notes:

 Run on a GPU machine: importing the model code initializes attention/MoE kernels.
 If another `veomni` is installed in the environment, the training entrypoint refuses to start rather than train on it. The launchers set `PYTHONPATH=:/VeOmni`; do the same if you invoke `tasks/train_sft.py` directly.
 `flash-attn` is needed only by the AToken tokenizer (anything that encodes or decodes images/video/3D). `liger-kernel` and `xformers` are not required.
 Object-storage packages (`petrel-oss-sdk` / `boto3`) are optional; local token files need neither.
 The driver changes into the repository root before launching Python, so relative paths resolve there. Set `LUMINA_ROOT=/path/to/InternLumina-U2` to call it from elsewhere; direct Python entrypoints want absolute paths. [...] ## ✨ Highlights

1. One model for omni-visual understanding, image generation and editing. Text QA, T2I generation, image understanding (VQA / OCR / chart / math reasoning), instruction-based image editing, video understanding and 3D understanding all run through the same backbone and the same discrete token interface.

results.title: Intern Lumina U2: Unified Model for Multimodal Content Creation | Welcome.AI
results.content:
## Executive Summary

The research introduces Intern Lumina U2, a novel model designed for unified multimodal generation, which combines text, images, and videos into a single framework. This model aims to address the limitations of existing approaches that either focus on discrete visual tokenizers or hybrid methods that can complicate the optimization process due to differences in how text and images are represented. [...] Intern Lumina U2 represents a significant advancement in this area by being the first diffusion language model to utilize multi-codebook visual tokens in a fully discrete space. This means that each visual element is represented by multiple codes drawn from different codebooks, enhancing its representational ability while still integrating seamlessly with text modeling techniques. The model processes visual and textual data simultaneously, which could lead to more efficient data handling and improved output quality.
